newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse suspends trading in Horizon shares.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse suspends trading in Horizon shares.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) suspended trading in the shares of research and development company Horizon-Multiplan for November 14, the BSE said in a statement on Thursday.
The BSE decided to suspend trading in the shares to protect the interest of investors who may have not received important information about the company's expected 1996 results.

On Thursday two Hungarian dailies published certain information about Horizon-Multiplan based on the company's statement, while the official bourse gazette received the information too late to publish it on Thursday.
Horizon-Multiplan informed the BSE in a fax dated November 13 that the two board meetings on November 6 and 13 reviewed the company's performance and modified the 1996 business plan, the BSE said.
"According to this information the company estimates its sales revenues to 130 million to 145 million forints in 1996," the BSE's statement said.
"Due to substantial extra marketing costs and lower (than planned) sales revenue the company expects 75 million to 85 million forints of losses by the end of the year," it added.
The BSE's statement said that Horizon-Multiplan promised to publish a statement about the board decisions in the bourse's gazette on November 15, making investors' access to information equal.
